extractions.quote: A woman aged 31 years with an uneventful family and medical history developed a slowly progressive stiffness and rigidity in axial muscles 10 years earlier. She had painful muscle spasms triggered by tactile and emotional stimuli, partial complex seizures, and paroxysmal autonomic dysfunction with tachycardia, hyperidrosis, and itch attacks. Clinical examination showed hyperlordosis of the lumbar spine. The muscular tone was markedly increased in the paraspinal region and proximally in the lower limbs. Spontaneous and touch-sensitive flexor spasms of the arms and legs were present. Deep tendon reflexes were normal and symmetric with flexor plantar responses. An EMG showed continuous electric activity at rest in the thoracoabdominal muscles. SPS was then diagnosed, and diazepam treatment was started (50 mg/d) with temporary response.

After a good response to baclofen treatment, she became pregnant. All drugs were discontinued with a subsequent clinical deterioration. At the 20th week of pregnancy, a sample of amnion and blood from the funiculus was taken, and anti-GAD65 was detected in the amniotic fluid and fetal and maternal serum. At the 39th week, the newborn was delivered by cesarean section. Clinical and neurologic examinations of the newborn were normal. A week after delivery, drugs were successfully started again. Two years later, the patient entered her second pregnancy, and treatment was discontinued. Although she worsened, she delivered a second healthy newborn at the 40th week.
